root_cause: The Pikaday date picker's keyboard handler (_onKeyChange) does not handle the Tab key (keyCode 9). When a user types a date in the bound input field and presses Tab, the picker remains open and its focusable elements (previous/next month navigation buttons and day buttons) intercept the Tab navigation, preventing focus from moving to the next form field (guests). The picker's aria-label instructs users to 'Use the arrow keys to pick a date', confirming that Tab should not be used for internal picker navigation.
repair_strategy: Add tabindex="-1" to all focusable buttons within the picker (pika-prev, pika-next, pika-day) so they are removed from the sequential tab order. Add a case for keyCode 9 (Tab) in the _onKeyChange switch statement: when Tab is pressed while the bound input field is focused (e.target === opts.field), hide the picker to release its focus trap and allow the browser's default Tab behavior to move focus to the next form field. This follows the APG date picker pattern and preserves native browser focus behavior.

expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can tab from the checkin date input field directly to the guests field (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.3 Focus Order). The picker's internal controls are no longer in the tab order; arrow keys on the input field navigate dates per the aria-label. Focus order follows DOM order naturally.
functional_risks: Low - only removes picker buttons from tab order; arrow key navigation via input field unchanged
Date selection via keyboard (Tab to day button + Enter) was not previously supported; direct input typing and arrow key navigation remain
verification_requirements: Tab from checkin field moves focus to guests field
